target_customer: Patients and consumers needing copies of medical records, plus businesses such as law firms and researchers; paid per record
problem: Getting medical records out of hospitals was slow, mostly by fax, and records were scattered across providers.
business_model: Per-request fee (about $30 per record per a secondary source) with a plan to build a unified patient record

founders.name: Feridun Mert Celebi
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; the page gives no background. Search coverage says the founders met at Yale.

founders.name: Paul Fletcher-Hill
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the YC launch post dated 2016-08-10, which says the co-founders graduated from Yale. Other co-founders named in a Wikipedia snippet (Kevin Grassi, Graham Kaemmer) were not confirmed on a source I opened.

exit.reason: Company announced the product would close on January 12, 2018 (company Medium post, seen only in a search snippet because the page returned 403). No cause stated in what I could read.

technical_complexity.rationale: The hard part was operations: faxing and phoning thousands of hospitals and digitizing records, not software. The YC post describes a contact database of over 2.5 million offices and security via Aptible.

defensibility.rationale: A contact database and hospital turnaround data helped, but record retrieval was a labor process others could copy, and established release-of-information vendors existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat was found. The product closed in January 2018.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites founder frustration obtaining records and reports over 10,000 records collected from over 2,300 hospitals since October 2015, with turnaround around ten days, about three times faster than average.

branding.domain_note: Wikipedia and aggregator profiles list patientbank.us; no .com ownership found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that conveyed the idea of a bank for patient records, but little press about the brand itself and the product closed after about two years.

outcome_analysis: PatientBank showed early traction with more than 10,000 records pulled from 2,300 hospitals and raised a 2.2 million dollar seed in December 2016 from General Catalyst and Khosla. It shut the product on 2018-01-12. The company's own reason could not be read, and the only cause on offer is a low-reliability case-study blog citing cash and monetization, so failure factors are tentative and rest on a labor-heavy per-record model.
notes: No company website listed in the directory. Competitors: the YC post names none, and available lists (Craft.co, a failure blog) are undated or low reliability, so the list is left empty; established release-of-information vendors existed but no dated source was found. Seed round rests on mobihealthnews and HIT Consultant snippets plus CB Insights (total 2.32M, so about 120K may be other funding, perhaps YC). The shutdown date comes from a search snippet of the company's own post. Reason for failure is not public in sources I could read.
